metadata.purpose: Canonical decision contract for three-dragon formation recommendations and multi-formation portfolios.
metadata.policy: Hard eligibility and evidence constraints are applied before comparative judgment. Strategic weights remain scenario-dependent and are not a universal tier score.

required_context.unknown_policy: Proceed with explicit assumptions when missing inputs do not prevent a useful conditional answer; identify the single missing input most likely to reverse the result.

portfolio_contract.default_rule: An unqualified request for two or more formations, armies, marches, or compositions means one simultaneously deployable portfolio with no dragon reused across formations.
portfolio_contract.independent_matchup_rule: Use independent_matchups only when the user explicitly requests separate hypothetical matchup answers whose dragons need not be deployed simultaneously.
portfolio_contract.allocation_rule: Select the complete portfolio globally from the full legal candidate set. Do not choose one formation, remove its dragons, and rerun greedily.
portfolio_contract.heterogeneous_group_rule: When ordered subsets of a deployable portfolio have different objectives, hard eligibility rules, or explicit preferences, encode them as portfolio_groups. Apply each group's constraints before ranking and allocate all group slots jointly; do not validate the request with a single global objective followed by a manual audit.
portfolio_contract.shared_affinity_default: Prefer 3-of-3 positive affinity for the formation's one shared troop. Compare a lower-affinity formation against the highest-synergy hard-constraint-eligible 3-of-3 candidate with the same competitive qualification; permit it only when its documented synergy advantage exceeds the missing-affinity count. When no such candidate exists, disclose that no perfect comparator is available rather than asserting a synergy override. For grouped portfolios this candidate-level comparison does not establish a feasible substitute for the complete disjoint allocation. Use minimum_positive_affinities: 3 when the caller requires affinity-perfect formations without exception.

auto_endgame_threshold.basis: A roster with enough mature dragons to field three developed armies is treated as endgame unless the caller explicitly selects unrestricted evaluation.

competitive_viability.ordinary_combat_rare_policy: In endgame ordinary-combat recommendations, a Rare dragon is strategically unqualified unless it has a reviewed exception or the caller explicitly allows unproven Rare use. This is a deployment-context gate, not a claim that rarity alone measures strength.
competitive_viability.siege_exception: Rare dragons remain eligible when the requested objective or selected shared troop is Siege; this exception does not carry into ordinary combat.
competitive_viability.fallback_rule: Retain strategically unqualified candidates in the audit. Select one only when no qualified candidate or complete qualified portfolio exists, and mark the result strategically unqualified.
competitive_viability.unknown_power_rule: When endgame Power is not comparable and a complete legal disjoint expert portfolio exists, use that expert portfolio as the conservative default. Preserve the mechanically ranked portfolio as an alternative rather than claiming it supersedes expert evidence.

decision_flow.rule: Remove unowned dragons, locked Habits, unavailable Vanguard effects, and content excluded by lifecycle policy before assigning synergy or counter credit.

Define the objective and, for counters, inventory material enemy threat instances by source, damage category, trigger, timing, target scope, and exclusions. A general-purpose meta evaluation does not require a named opponent; assess broad formation value and explicitly state the opposing troop type that has advantage over the selected shared troop.

Do not stop at the first plausible trio. Build a candidate ledger before choosing: for ordinary combat recommendations retain every legal common baseline from data/common_formations.json, the strongest affinity-perfect line found for each available non-Siege troop type, the strongest explicit producer/payoff line, the strongest objective-specific line, and a counter-specific line when an enemy is known. Applicability affects the comparison but does not remove a legal common baseline. A single line may satisfy multiple categories, but every retained line must be evaluated under the same progression and evidence gates.

Trace producer-to-payoff chains only through abilities active at the reported Star rank, level, and Habit skill level. Dragon Level never grants Stars: Stars increase only through dragon-specific Relics from opened Dragon Chests and unlock Habits at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 Stars. Breedmarks and rarity-matched Cores upgrade unlocked Habits separately. For the same dragon, a higher Star rank expands or preserves its eligible kit and can unlock additional synergies; do not turn that into a cross-dragon ranking. Unknown Habit skill level means unknown value or reliability, not Level 1 or maximum.

When Dragon Levels are known, compare a capacity proxy using the recorded level curve plus the confirmed account-level Dragon's Army bonus. Disclose the recorded Star scalar but do not apply it until a complete final-stat formula is independently established. Treat Troop Capacity as a practical health-pool input, not as casualty prevention by itself. For troop-preservation objectives, first protect the weakest lane with its per-dragon capacity floor; then compare documented preservation tier from active Recovery, Protect, Resistance, Evade, Cleanse, explicit mitigation, trigger certainty, target coverage, negative side effects, and known Habit investment; then compare total capacity and exact preservation score.
Choose exactly one Vanguard after comparing all three Vanguard abilities, then honor directional flank beneficiaries and exact target scopes.

Choose one troop type for the trio. Before calling any type affinity-perfect, compute the exact intersection of the three dragons' canonical positive-affinity sets; only types in that intersection qualify. Evaluate all three positive and negative affinities separately from enemy troop advantage and objective-specific Siege value.
Classify pivotal effects on trigger certainty and prerequisites, use the actual Habit skill track, and compare opening Rounds 1-10 with later cycles when sustained combat is plausible.

Compare the leading line with every legal common baseline and with the strongest other credible alternative. A common baseline can itself be the leading line and final recommendation. Preserve a defensible alternative when evidence does not establish one winner; state the assumption that would reverse the choice.

candidate_search.full_roster_ledger: When the full roster is in scope and Power is unknown or comparable, inspect every eligible dragon before finalizing the shortlist. For each non-Siege troop type, retain the strongest credible affinity-perfect trio if one exists; separately retain the strongest explicit synergy and objective-specific trios even when they overlap.
candidate_search.common_baselines: Load data/common_formations.json for every formation recommendation. For ordinary combat, retain each common formation whose three dragons and shared troop type are legal under the user's roster and progression. Treat applicability as objective and matchup evidence, not as a prefilter. Recompute each line under actual inputs rather than assuming the reference Level 50, 6-Star, Level-5 state. A specialized non-combat or Siege-only request may mark a combat baseline inapplicable only with an explicit reason.
candidate_search.common_baseline_eligibility: A common formation is an ordinary fully eligible candidate, never a control group that must lose. Do not exclude, down-rank, or omit it because it is a baseline; recommend it directly when the same evidence-based comparison shows it is the best-supported line.
candidate_search.common_baseline_fairness: Expert-recommended status is positive formation-level evidence, not immunity from legality, progression, troop, matchup, or mechanics gates. Recompute each expert line under the user's actual inputs. When endgame Power is unknown, a complete legal expert portfolio is the conservative default; known comparable Power or material matchup evidence may displace it.
candidate_search.lane_permutations: For every retained trio, compare all legal Vanguard choices and directional flank beneficiaries before selecting its best lane order.
candidate_search.pairwise_comparison: Compare retained lines pairwise on the objective profile, unlocked mechanics, reliability, lane value, shared affinity, timing, and known matchup. Record the decisive advantage and material reversal condition internally; do not claim a full-roster optimum from an unreported preselection heuristic.
candidate_search.cross_objective_check: If the same line wins materially different objectives, explicitly verify why the changed objective does not alter the ordering. A generic hybrid must not win attack and survivability prompts merely because it is broadly competent.
candidate_search.benchmark_safety: Evaluation-only benchmark answers must not seed, boost, or exempt a trio. The formations in data/common_formations.json carry an independently recorded user-confirmed expert recommendation prior and therefore may influence selection only through that disclosed evidence class.

visible_power.meaning: Player-specific current viability signal incorporating progression not fully represented by canonical mechanics.
visible_power.use: Apply as a viability anchor and a strong comparison factor among candidates capable of the required job. It does not create missing counter coverage or unlock mechanics.
visible_power.required_disclosure: Explain any omission of a materially higher-Power candidate.

counter_coverage_states.direct: Explicit wording applies to the exact threat instance.
counter_coverage_states.partial: Explicit wording covers only part of the damage category, timing, target set, or trigger.
counter_coverage_states.probabilistic: Coverage depends on a chance-based trigger or uncertain prerequisite.
counter_coverage_states.none: No explicit applicable response; broad role similarity earns no counter credit.

anti_overfitting.benchmark_rule: Use evaluation-only expert answers to diagnose general knowledge, mechanics, search, weighting, context, or presentation gaps; never add formation-name exceptions. Canonical common baselines are independently declared in data/common_formations.json and remain subject to ordinary evidence comparison.
anti_overfitting.holdout_rule: For each meaningful rule change, test at least one variation that changes a lane, troop matchup, Star/Habit gate, Power relationship, or enemy threat.
anti_overfitting.alternative_rule: Do not force benchmark agreement when repository evidence supports a defensible alternative.
